data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word 'Tabatha', meaning 'gift from God'. In the New Testament, a woman named Tabitha, also known as Dorcas, was a disciple who was revered for her good works and charitable deeds. After her death, she was brought back to life by Peter. The name Tabatha carries the meaning “Given by God” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Tabatha usually hope their child will grow to embody given by god and live with faith, good character and purpose.

It was a name given to girls to denote the notion of a 'gift from God'. The name's association with good works and charitable deeds became an inspiration and representation of the ideal Christian woman.
data.spiritual_significance: Symbolically, the name 'Tabatha' embodies the divine essence of Christian faith. It represents the belief that every individual is a gift from God, and is meant to contribute in their unique way to the betterment of the world. The spiritual significance of the name Tabatha is further emphasized in the New Testament story where Peter brings Tabitha back to life after her death, reminding us of the eternal and sacred power of God.
